name: kb_capabilities
description: Read-only: what the calling session's project KB serves, in the shape of the KB server's GET /api/kb/capabilities body {contract, routes, branch_aware, query_filters?}. Under an http KB provider it returns the server's body as-is (route names this fleet server does not call and extra fields included), except that a malformed query_filters (not an array of strings) is dropped and treated as absent; a server without the capabilities route (404/501) yields the default set (every route except demote and withdraw, branch_aware false, no query_filters); a partially-typed body fails with E-KB-HTTP-UNSUPPORTED, a 5xx/429 with E-KB-HTTP-UNREACHABLE. Under a SQLite KB it returns the local implementation: contract v1, every route (demote and withdraw included), branch_aware false, query_filters files and symbols. Never mutates anything and never bumps use_count. Scope: always the calling session's own KB -- a member session uses its registered work folder; any other session uses the first MCP client root (roots/list) inside a git repository with an origin remote, as that repository's top level, or the fleet server's working folder when the client offers no roots; there is no repo/path scope argument (the removed repo_path, repo and repo_remote_url keys fail with E-SCOPE-KEY-REMOVED). Fails with E-SELF-NO-WORKFOLDER, E-SELF-NOT-A-REPO or E-SELF-NO-REMOTE (each with a one-line remediation) when that folder cannot carry a KB identity (it must be a git repository with an origin remote).
